problem: Patients say they left messages and never got an appointment.
walkthrough: A patient calls and usually leaves a voicemail after hours. The next morning the receptionist listens to the voicemails. She writes each request on a sticky note. Then she calls the patient back to book a time in the scheduling system. If the patient doesn't answer, the note just sits on her desk.

answers.trigger: Patients call and leave a voicemail.
answers.completion: Once it's in the scheduling system we consider it done.
answers.exceptions: The sticky note just sits there until someone notices.
answers.waiting: We wait for the patient to call us back.
answers.decisions: No real decisions, we just book the first open slot.

Then he types the measurements into our quoting spreadsheet. The office manager emails the quote to the customer. After that it's whoever remembers to follow up.

answers.completion: I don't know, we never really close them.
answers.exceptions: Nothing happens, it just gets forgotten.
answers.waiting: We wait for Carlos to have a free afternoon to measure.
answers.decisions: Carlos decides the price based on experience.

problem: Custom cake orders get mixed up and a few were missed entirely.
walkthrough: Customers message us on Instagram with what they want. I copy the order details into a paper order book. Then Priya checks the order book every morning and bakes the cakes due that week. When the cake is picked up, the customer pays at the counter.

answers.completion: It's done when they pick it up and pay.
answers.exceptions: If Priya misses it in the book, we find out when the customer shows up.
answers.waiting: Sometimes we wait on the customer to confirm the design.
answers.decisions: Priya decides if we can fit it in.

handoffs.text: She just checks the book when she gets in.

problem: New clients complain onboarding takes weeks.
walkthrough: A new client signs the engagement letter. Then our admin emails them a checklist of documents to send. We wait until they upload everything to the portal. Jamal reviews the documents and enters the details into our tax software. Finally the partner approves the file before we start work.

answers.trigger: It starts when the client signs the engagement letter.
answers.completion: When the partner approves the file, onboarding is done and we mark it complete in the tax software.
answers.exceptions: If documents are missing, the admin emails them again, sometimes three or four times.
answers.waiting: We wait on the client to upload documents.
answers.decisions: The partner approves each file.

handoffs.text: The portal emails Jamal when an upload arrives.
Jamal puts it in the partner review queue in the tax software.

problem: Customers keep calling to ask whether their car estimate is ready.
walkthrough: The customer drops off the car and describes the problem to the service writer. The service writer writes the complaint on a paper repair order. A mechanic inspects the car and tells the service writer what it needs. The service writer types the estimate into the shop software and calls the customer for approval.

answers.trigger: The customer drops off the car.
answers.completion: When the customer approves, we mark the repair order approved in the shop software.
answers.exceptions: If the customer doesn't pick up, we try again the next day, if someone remembers.
answers.waiting: We wait for the mechanic to finish the inspection, and then for the customer to approve.
answers.decisions: The mechanic decides what repairs are needed.

handoffs.text: The mechanic tells the service writer at the counter.
